blocks.content: As previewed in the Pod Scheduling Basics topic, nodeSelector is the simplest way to constrain where a Pod can be scheduled, a straightforward, exact label match, this topic covers it, and its real limitations, in full.
nodeSelector is a plain map of labels a node must carry for a Pod to be scheduled onto it, no operators, no weighting, no complexity, just an exact match requirement.

blocks.alt: The most straightforward scheduling constraint Kubernetes offers

blocks.content:
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    disktype: ssd
    zone: us-east-1a

blocks.content: There is no fuzzy or partial matching here, a node either has the exact label key and value specified, or it does not, nodeSelector offers no way to express anything more nuanced than that.

blocks.alt: A precise, exact match, with no room for nuance

blocks.content: When several labels are specified, every single one must match, there is no way to say "either this label or that one," nodeSelector only supports requiring all specified constraints simultaneously.

blocks.alt: Every specified label must match, with no OR option available

blocks.content: Two common real needs fall outside what nodeSelector can do at all: expressing "this label OR that label" (an either/or condition), and expressing "prefer this, but still schedule the Pod even if it is not available" (a soft, non-mandatory preference).

blocks.alt: Two genuinely common needs, neither expressible with this alone

blocks.content: 5. Where the More Expressive Tool Lives
blocks.text: 5. Where the More Expressive Tool Lives

blocks.content: Exactly these two limitations are what Node Affinity, covered in the very next topic, exists to solve, a strictly more expressive superset of what nodeSelector can do.

blocks.alt: The exact gap the next topic, Node Affinity, is built to close

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: nodeSelector is the simplest scheduling constraint, an exact label match with only AND logic between multiple labels.
It cannot express OR conditions or soft preferences, the exact gap Node Affinity, covered next, is designed to fill.
